title: AI-assisted workflows with Claude Code
task_statement: Run Claude Code in scripts and CI with bounded tools, checkable results, and a clear trigger. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Headless runs
components.first_principle: A print mode run returns a result and an exit status, so a script can decide whether the job passes.

nodes.label: JSON result with session ID and cost

steps: Run claude with the -p flag to start a non-interactive run.
Pass --tools with only the built-in tools the job needs, such as Read and Edit.
Pass --allowedTools to approve those tools without a prompt.
Add --bare in CI to skip hooks, skills, and CLAUDE.md files from the host.
Choose --output-format json to read the result, the session ID, and the cost.
Check the exit status before the job continues. Zero means the run succeeded.
Run the team test command as a separate step. (Inference)
pros: A script runs Claude Code without an interactive session.
The JSON output includes the total cost, so a script can record spend.
The --tools flag restricts which built-in tools the run can use.
cons: Without --bare, a print run runs project hooks and connects project MCP servers, even in an untrusted folder.
A print run shows no workspace trust dialog and no per-server approval prompt.
Piped stdin has a size cap, so large inputs need a file path in the prompt.
The --allowedTools flag only removes prompts. It does not restrict which tools are available.
use_when: A CI job needs a model result with a clear pass or fail status.
A script needs output that matches a JSON Schema.
do_not_use_when: A task needs a person to approve each step in real time. (Inference)
A developer needs a one-off answer, and an interactive session fits better.

constraints.choice: Pass --tools to restrict the built-in tools, and --allowedTools to approve them without a prompt.
constraints.combination: Use the dontAsk permission mode for a locked-down CI run, so any call that would prompt is denied.

constraints.choice: Read the exit status and the result field before the job passes.
constraints.combination: Record total_cost_usd from the JSON output for each run.

constraints.choice: Track spend with total_cost_usd for each run.
constraints.combination: When a run continues a conversation, the total includes the earlier runs.

constraints.choice: Add --bare when the repository is not trusted.
Add --bare in CI so host skills and subagents do not load.
constraints.combination: Omit --bare only in a trusted checkout when the job needs project hooks or skills. (Inference)

native_services.text: The GitHub Action can use Amazon Bedrock with the use_bedrock input set to true.
Claude Code reads CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY and the other Foundry variables from the environment, which suits a scripted run.

components.exam_tie: D7.2. Expect a scenario with a CI check or a scripted call. The credited answer uses a bounded print run with a fixed tools list and a checked exit status. (Inference)
components.trap: An --allowedTools list read as a tool restriction. The flag only auto-approves the listed tools. To restrict which tools exist, use --tools, and bypass mode belongs only in isolated environments.
components.decision_rule: Restrict each scripted run with --tools, approve only those tools, and check the exit status before the job passes.
components.exam_tip: If the stem asks to restrict tools in a CI run, look for --tools or a deny rule, not --allowedTools alone.

key_facts.text: Claude Code exits with code 0 on success and a non-zero code when the run fails.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The JSON output payload includes total_cost_usd and a per-model cost breakdown.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The --bare flag skips auto-discovery of hooks, skills, subagents, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, and CLAUDE.md.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Without --bare, a print run runs project hooks and connects .mcp.json servers in an untrusted folder.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The --json-schema flag returns output in the structured_output field.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The --allowedTools flag lets tools run without a prompt. To restrict which tools are available, use --tools.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.label: Fact

components.name: GitHub Actions workflows
components.first_principle: A workflow trigger starts Claude Code in the repository, and repository secrets hold the credential.
steps: Install the Claude GitHub App on the repository.
Add the authentication secret as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY or CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN.
Copy the workflow file into the .github/workflows folder.
Mention @claude in an issue or pull request comment to start a run in interactive mode.
Review the pull request that the action opens before you merge it. (Inference)
pros: The action runs in the repository and uses the repository permissions it receives. (Inference)
The quick setup command writes the secret and the workflow files for you.
A federated credential needs no stored long-lived secret.
cons: An OAuth token belongs to the subscription of the person who ran the setup command.
Each repository needs its own secret unless the team shares an organization secret.
A workflow that runs on every comment can start more runs than the team expects. (Inference)
use_when: The team wants a comment on an issue or pull request to start a model run.
The team wants the run output to appear as a pull request.
do_not_use_when: A developer wants a local result, and a headless run fits better.
The secret must outlive one developer, and an API key from the console fits better.

constraints.choice: Use an API key from the Claude Console for a secret shared across repositories.
constraints.combination: Use an organization-level Actions secret so repositories share one copy.

constraints.choice: Store the credential as a repository secret, never in the workflow file.
constraints.combination: Use workload identity federation to avoid a stored long-lived secret.

constraints.choice: Use interactive mode with the default @claude trigger when a person starts each run.
constraints.combination: Set a prompt input when the workflow must run without a comment.

constraints.choice: Grant the workflow only the permissions it needs. (Inference)
constraints.combination: Grant id-token write for the federation exchange, even with a custom token.

native_services.text: The GitHub Action can run through Amazon Bedrock, with the use_bedrock input.

native_services.service: Claude Models on Google Cloud (Google managed)
native_services.text: The GitHub Action can run through Google Cloud's Agent Platform with the use_vertex input set to true.
The GitHub Action can run through Microsoft Foundry with the use_foundry input set to true.

components.exam_tie: D7.2. Expect a scenario where a team wants an agent to act on a comment or an issue. The credited answer uses the GitHub Action with a repository secret and a pull request as output. (Inference)
components.trap: A personal subscription token stored as a shared organization secret. The docs say the token is tied to the subscription of the person who created it, so an API key fits a shared secret.
components.decision_rule: Use the GitHub Action for a repository trigger, and use an API key for a secret that several repositories share.
components.exam_tip: If the stem names a shared secret across repositories, choose an API key over an OAuth token.

components.name: Subagent roles for review and exploration
components.first_principle: A subagent with a narrow tools list can explore or review without the power to change files.
steps: Create a subagent file in the .claude/agents folder for the team.
Set the tools field to Read and Grep for an exploration role.
Set the model field to haiku for a lower-cost exploration role.
Ask the main session to delegate the review to the subagent. (Inference)
Check the findings for file and line references before you act on them. (Inference)
pros: A subagent keeps long search output out of the main conversation.
A tools list removes write access for a review role.
The team commits the subagent file, so each clone gets the same role.
cons: A subagent without a tools field inherits every tool available to subagents.
Plugin subagents ignore the hooks, mcpServers, and permissionMode fields.
Rewind usually does not restore subagent edits to other files, so use Git to revert them.
use_when: A repository review needs file references from a read-only role.
An exploration task reads many files that the main session does not need.
do_not_use_when: The task is one file edit that the main session can do directly.
The role must enforce a permission that only a settings rule can enforce.

constraints.choice: Give an exploration role only the Read and Grep tools.
constraints.combination: Add disallowedTools for a write tool when a role inherits tools.

constraints.choice: Set the model field to haiku for exploration.
constraints.combination: Use the inherit value when the role must match the main session model.

constraints.choice: Commit project subagents in .claude/agents so the team reviews them.
constraints.combination: Deploy a managed subagent file when the organization needs the same role everywhere.

constraints.choice: Split large reviews into one subagent per area of the repository. (Inference)

components.exam_tie: D7.2. Expect a scenario that asks for an agent role with least privilege. The credited answer sets a tools list on the subagent file. (Inference)
components.trap: A review subagent with no tools field, which inherits write tools. The role then can edit files that a review should only read.
components.decision_rule: Set the tools field on each role to the smallest set that the role needs.
components.exam_tip: If a stem asks for a read-only reviewer, look for a tools list that omits write tools.

key_facts.text: A subagent without a tools field inherits every tool available to subagents.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: A user or project subagent named Explore overrides the built-in Explore subagent.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Plugin subagents do not support the hooks, mcpServers, or permissionMode frontmatter fields.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: Managed subagent definitions take precedence over project and user subagents with the same name.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The model field accepts sonnet, opus, haiku, fable, a full model ID, or inherit.
key_facts.label: Fact

decision_flow:
flowchart TD
  A{Does a script or CI job need the result?} -->|Yes| B{Is the trigger a comment or issue?}
  A -->|No| I[Interactive session]
  B -->|Yes| G[GitHub Action with repository secret]
  B -->|No| H[Headless print run with tools list]
  H --> J{Does the job parse fields?}
  J -->|Yes| K[JSON output with schema]
  J -->|No| L[Text output with exit status check]
cheatsheet:
flowchart LR
  P[print run -p] --> T[Tools flag restricts]
  P --> E[Exit status]
  P --> O[JSON output]
  O --> C[Cost field]
  G[GitHub Action] --> S[Repository secret]
  S --> K[API key for shared use]
  R[Subagent] --> RT[Read and Grep only]
